title: Reset checked items into chronological checking order
environment: Current phone build; exact mode and persistence conditions still to be recorded.
reproduction_status: Corrected regressions fail the previous local implementation at model, QML and native Android levels. The final implementation passes the chronological order and unchecked-prefix requirements, including pending edits, repeated Reset and restart persistence.
reproduction: Start with unchecked items in the order 1, 2, 3.
Check item 3, then item 1, then item 2, identifying each by its name rather than its changing row index.
Invoke Reset checks from the drawer.
Inspect the unchecked order immediately and when the list is used again.
actual: The previous implementation clears checkmarks while retaining newest-first checked stack order, so checked 2,1,3 resets to 2,1,3 rather than the corrected expected 3,1,2.
expected: Reverse checked positions into chronological checking order and clear all flags, leaving unchecked entries in place. Initial 1,2,3 checked as 3,1,2 becomes checked 2,1,3 and resets to unchecked 3,1,2. Mixed unchecked A,B before checked C,D resets to A,B,D,C. Preserve IDs, draft text, free insertion point, and persistence; a repeated Reset must not reverse again.
impact: The user must reorder a reusable shopping list after resetting it, disrupting the intended workflow. Severity described as major.
source_notes: The checked stack is newest first. Reset must reverse only its checked slots to recover chronological checking order; do not reverse the unchecked prefix or the whole list.

An edited checked item is represented by its editor placeholder and m_pendingEdit. Include that placeholder in the reversal while keeping its draft and identity, then clear the pending original checked flag.
Use existing Model.move with Save::NO for endpoint swaps; it emits proper row moves and updates editorIndex. Avoid resetting the whole model, which would recreate delegates and lose draft text.

Clear flags while collecting checked positions, reverse those positions and save once if any checked positions were found. Ordinary single-item correction still uses setChecked and retains nearby first-in/last-out correction.
Earlier local work and ui009-* reports without revised followed a superseded instruction to preserve the entire visible order. The user correction and mixed-list answer replace that policy.
acceptance_criteria: Initial 1,2,3 checked as 3,1,2 produces checked 2,1,3 and resets to unchecked 3,1,2.
Unchecked A,B followed by checked C,D resets to A,B,D,C, retaining unchecked entries first.
All flags are cleared, including a checked item being edited; retain its draft and original identity through movement.
Keep a free editor insertion point in place while reversing checked slots.
The result survives switching lists, saving, reopening and cold restart.
Repeated Reset leaves the already-reset order unchanged.
Verify the actual drawer action with failing-before/passing-after model, QML and native Android regression coverage.
evidence: User report and explicit 1,2,3 / check 3,1,2 / reset 2,1,3 example in the QShopper development chat on 2026-10-28.
clarification: 2026-10-29: user corrected the original expected order to chronological checking order (first checked becomes first reset), then specified mixed lists retain unchecked items first: A,B,C,D with C,D checked resets to A,B,D,C.

implementation.change: Collect checked row positions and clear their flags, including a checked item being edited. Reverse the recorded pairs with existing row moves, then save once. Unchecked slots and free editor position remain fixed; a pending draft follows its item.

regression_tests.after: All seven targeted records pass offscreen and with native Windows rendering. Five cases cover the main sequence, mixed lists and editing each checked position, preserving text through row movement, repeated Reset and a fresh main window.

regression_tests.before: The native checking sequence produces 2,1,3; the previous APK fails the corrected Reset expectation of 3,1,2.
regression_tests.coverage: Native swipes, double taps and drawer Reset for the main example, mixed unchecked prefix, pending edit, repeat Reset, draft retention and cold-restart order/flag/identity preservation.
regression_tests.after: All 13 native checks pass: exact and pending cases reset to 3,1,2; the mixed case resets to A,B,3,1,2. Flags clear, drafts survive, repeated Reset is unchanged and cold restart preserves order/flags/IDs.
